clue.text: Famous old Hollywood actress, good in the last act

parts.note: Gloria Swanson, silent-era star of Sunset Boulevard

explanation.surface: A faded film star is said to deliver her finest performance in the closing act.
explanation.definitionFit: A swan song is a final performance or farewell effort, after the legend that swans sing only before dying.

clue.text: This may stop one from getting off

definitions.text: This may stop one from getting off

parts.words: This may stop one from getting off
parts.note: 'getting off' suggests leaving a bus or train, but here it means getting off to sleep, which sleeplessness prevents

explanation.surface: Something that might keep a passenger from alighting at their stop.
explanation.definitionFit: Chronic sleeplessness is what keeps a person from nodding off at night.

clue.text: Stop working to phone one close to apoplexy about wrong data

parts.note: to call someone is to phone them

indicators.note: the pair of pieces goes around the scrambled letters, so 'about' signals one enclosing the other

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: the close of a word is its final letter, taken here from apoplexy
data set wrong is data with its letters rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone near a fit over faulty figures decides to phone in and finish for the day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' wraps one and the end of apoplexy around the rearranged data, I at the front and Y at the back; 'Stop working' looks like an instruction but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Calling it a day is an idiom for ceasing work, usually until tomorrow.

clue.text: More theatrical, one pitching a tent?

definitions.meaning: comparative of camp, meaning exaggerated and showy
a person who goes camping and puts up a tent

explanation.surface: A question about whether a showier person is the one putting up the canvas.
explanation.definitionFit: Camp means theatrically exaggerated, so its comparative fits; separately a holidaymaker under canvas is a camper.

clue.text: Kipling's fourth poem on English existence

indicators.note: the fourth letter of the surname Kipling is taken

parts.note: 'If-' is Kipling's best-known poem

explanation.surface: Reads like a literature note on a Kipling poem about English existence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'If-' is Rudyard Kipling's famous poem of stoic advice to a son, much loved in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: Existence and being alive are close synonyms, as in 'the meaning of existence'.

clue.text: Suggestive remark made by one nun I'd upset

indicators.note: letters upset are knocked out of order, so the phrase is rearranged

explanation.surface: A nun takes offence at a risque comment someone made.
explanation.definitionFit: An insinuation or veiled hint, typically a sexual double meaning, is exactly a suggestive remark.

clue.text: A coin from each one

parts.note: a piece is a coin, as in a fifty-pence piece

explanation.surface: A coin handed out to every person in turn.
explanation.definitionFit: Used adverbially, it means to or for every individual, as in 'a pound each'.

clue.text: Stick given a Democrat at this point

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for a US Democrat
here means at this place or point

explanation.surface: A walking stick passed to a Democrat on the spot.
explanation.definitionFit: To stick to something is to cling or hold fast to it, a straight verb synonym.

clue.text: Run west with American to find country

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for run
W is the compass abbreviation for west
and means together with

explanation.surface: Travel instructions: head west alongside an American to reach some nation.
explanation.definitionFit: Landlocked East African republic, a nation and hence a country.

clue.text: Staircase containing a new window

indicators.note: the stair word holds the other letters within it

parts.note: a flight of stairs is a staircase

explanation.surface: A stairwell with a freshly fitted window.
explanation.definitionFit: A fanlight is a semicircular window above a door, so it is one kind of window.

clue.text: Release a French pair

parts.note: un is French for a
a couple is a pair

explanation.surface: Letting a French couple go free.
explanation.definitionFit: To detach or disconnect linked things, such as railway carriages, is to set them free.

clue.text: Signal returned by her playing card game

indicators.note: returned means the signal word is sent back the other way

parts.note: a cue is a signal to begin, as given to an actor

indicators.note: playing suggests the letters of 'her' are fooling about out of order

explanation.surface: A cue comes back as she is in the middle of a game of cards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returned' turns CUE to EUC; 'playing' rearranges HER to HRE.
explanation.definitionFit: Euchre is a trick-taking game, once popular in North America, played with a short deck of cards.

clue.text: Plump bird associated with Christmas competition

parts.note: round means plump or rotund
the robin appears on British Christmas cards

explanation.surface: A fat festive bird is linked to some contest.
explanation.definitionFit: A tournament format in which every entrant plays each of the others in turn is a type of competition.

clue.text: Comic opera singer, expert on love

parts.note: a buff is an enthusiast or expert
love is nil in tennis, written as O

explanation.surface: A singer of comic opera who knows a great deal about love.
explanation.definitionFit: Italian term for a bass who sings comic roles in opera buffa.

clue.text: Chaperon perhaps agitated round rough oaf

indicators.note: agitated suggests the letters are stirred up into a new order

explanation.surface: A chaperone, flustered, fusses around a clumsy lout.
explanation.definitionFit: A ceremonial escort for a dignitary; a chaperone also escorts, hence 'perhaps' marking a loose example.

clue.text: Character, in middle of act, withdrew

indicators.note: the role word sits at the centre of the act word

parts.note: a deed is an act
a part is an actor's character

explanation.surface: An actor's character exits halfway through the act.
explanation.definitionFit: To depart is to leave or go away, so the past tense equals withdrew.

clue.text: Agency to pass on material

parts.note: an organ is a means or agency of action, as a newspaper is an organ of opinion
to pass on is a euphemism for to die

explanation.surface: An agency forwarding some cloth to someone else.
explanation.definitionFit: Organdie is a fine, stiff, translucent cotton fabric, so a material.

clue.text: Kept talking, heartlessly betrayed

indicators.note: heartlessly means the central letter of the phrase is cut out

parts.note: rattled on means chattered on at length

explanation.surface: Someone who wouldn't stop talking cruelly informed on a friend.
explanation.definitionFit: To rat on someone is slang for informing on or betraying them.

clue.text: 100 in number for printmaker

indicators.note: in places the numeral inside the anaesthetic

parts.note: crossword trick: number here is something that numbs, an anaesthetic such as ether
C is the Roman numeral for 100

explanation.surface: Reads as a count: a hundred out of some figure being for an artist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'number' is read as numb-er, a thing that numbs, not a figure.
explanation.definitionFit: An etcher makes prints from plates engraved with acid, so is a kind of printmaker.

clue.text: Stroke is worried before onset of squall

parts.note: cares means is concerned or worried

indicators.note: the onset of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A sailor frets about a stroke of bad weather as a squall begins.
explanation.definitionFit: To caress is to stroke gently and affectionately.

clue.text: Debauched scholar, student I confine to college grounds

parts.note: prof, short for professor, is a scholar
L is a learner driver's plate, so a student
at Oxford and Cambridge to gate a student is to confine them to college

explanation.surface: A dissolute academic and a student face being kept inside the college.
explanation.walkthrough: Gating is an Oxbridge punishment that confines an undergraduate within college.
explanation.definitionFit: A profligate person is recklessly dissolute, so debauched is a direct synonym.

clue.text: Thoughtlessness of tax involving computer services

indicators.note: involving means enfolding, so the tax word wraps the computing letters

parts.note: a levy is a tax
IT is information technology, computing services

explanation.surface: Careless thinking behind a tax on computing.
explanation.definitionFit: Levity is frivolity or lack of seriousness, close to a careless thoughtlessness.

clue.text: In with academics where Cornell is

indicators.note: In signals that the letters lie within the phrase that follows

explanation.surface: In among scholars is the location of a university.
explanation.definitionFit: Cornell University is in the city of Ithaca, New York.

clue.text: Suggests loans

definitions.meaning: to advance an idea is to put it forward or propose it
sums lent ahead of time, such as an advance on wages

explanation.surface: Proposing credit, as a lender might.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb puts ideas forward, and the noun names money paid ahead or lent.

clue.text: Member of the clergy caught out immediately

indicators.note: out means the letter for caught is left out

parts.note: a canon is a member of a cathedral's clergy
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A cleric is caught out straight away.
explanation.definitionFit: Anon is an old word meaning soon or at once, so immediately.

clue.text: Bully about to get a little time inside after that

indicators.note: inside means these letters go within the 'after that' word

parts.note: then means after that
re means about or concerning
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A bully is about to spend a short spell inside afterwards.
explanation.definitionFit: To bully someone is to intimidate them, which is to threaten as a verb.

clue.text: Picked up actress associated with Burton, maker of garments

indicators.note: picked up means heard, so the actress's name is taken by its sound

parts.note: Elizabeth Taylor twice married Richard Burton

explanation.surface: An actress linked to Burton was spotted with a clothes maker.
explanation.walkthrough: Burton is also a British menswear chain, which helps the misdirection.
explanation.definitionFit: A tailor makes clothes, especially suits, to measure.

clue.text: Trump's last official address in high office

indicators.note: the last letter of the name Trump is taken

parts.note: a residency is an official residence

explanation.surface: Where Trump officially lived during his time in the top job.
explanation.definitionFit: The office of president is a high office of state.
